examples.act: Kutuzov's headquarters at Krzenowitz, where the dispositions were read overnight. The emperors join the 4th Column on the plateau about 08:30-09:00
Formed near Augezd before first light
At the southern end of the Pratzen plateau
Attacks Telnitz; the village changes hands several times
Leaves its camp at seven, as the disposition ordered, and descends toward the Goldbach (Buxhowden's and Kutuzov's reports)
Feeding all three columns into the Goldbach villages
Storms Sokolnitz; Kamensky's brigade marches at the rear of the column

Langeron rides back and sends reinforcements up the slope toward Kamensky. The accounts name the Kursk regiment: Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky has Langeron bring it up too late, losing up to 1,600 men; Langeron's journal, as Sokolov quotes it, two of its battalions, half killed and half taken with their guns and colours; Schönhals has it left in reserve behind Sokolnitz and mostly taken there
Pushes into Telnitz behind Kienmayer

Spread along the crest from the Pratzeberg to Stare Vinohrady: Jurczek on the summit, Rottermund on the Old Vineyards. The accounts differ: Schönhals has the Austrians and Kamensky climb the height in a second bayonet attack before Boyer's dragoons drive them off; Thiébault has them dispersed by his guns
Headquarters falls back toward Krzenowitz
Rottermund's brigade falls back on Stare Vinohrady, then east
Falls back fighting as Blasowitz is lost (this map's sequence; Schönhals has its line broken later)

Its cavalry formed beyond the Telnitz defile, west of the Goldbach, its battalions and guns in Telnitz (Stutterheim; Schönhals), until the French came down behind the column. The point drawn, between Telnitz and the Satschan mere, is where Schönhals has Carneville's brigade face Vandamme's descent: this map's
Driven back toward Sokolnitz by Davout at about 12:30 (this map's reading; no account read gives it)
Escapes south over the Augezd defile

Back across the brook, withdrawing on Austerlitz, where the Tsar orders Miloradovich to hold the town (his report; Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky). The point, halfway from Krzenowitz to Austerlitz, is this map's
On the height toward Rausnitz, covering the Allied right (Schönhals); he retreats on Austerlitz about six in Schönhals, and is behind it by six in Stutterheim

On the height of his bivouac, taken here to be the Zuran: 'la butte' of the orders of 1 December, 'the barrow by Schlapanitz' in Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky. The dispositions call his marshals to his bivouac for the morning's orders
Standing in fog behind Puntowitz, which hid it from the plateau
Concealed by the fog in the valley behind Girzikowitz

At Raigern since the night of 1 December, 8 km south-west of Telnitz and just beyond the map edge, after about 115 km from Vienna in under two days in Sokolov, thirty-six leagues in forty-eight hours in Thiers, a march whose figures vary between the sources
Behind Girzikowitz on I Corps' left (Stutterheim; the 30th Bulletin for the left); the place drawn, west of the village, is this map's

Where I Corps stood at dawn is disputed: in the second line behind Soult on 1 December (Savary), behind Girzikowitz (Stutterheim), in the Goldbach ravine with Soult's troops (Marbot), across the brook since the evening before (Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky); the place drawn is this map's
Formed near the Zuran with the Guard
Contests Telnitz house by house against Kienmayer
Marching from Raigern toward Telnitz
Forms in the Goldbach valley for the attack
Forms in the Goldbach valley
Fights for Sokolnitz village and the castle wall

Behind Sokolnitz, on the left of Davout's line (Davout's report); Levasseur's brigade marches up onto the Pratzeberg from the Kobelnitz side: Schönhals has Soult send it, held in reserve, to support Saint-Hilaire's right, and Thiébault has it hidden between Kobelnitz and his brigade
Moves forward from the Zuran to Stare Vinohrady
Presses east to the stream at Sokolnitz as the trap closes

At the chapel of St Anthony above Augezd, having come from the Pratzen with the Guard cavalry and artillery (Schönhals; a French officer's note of 1806 has him come down to the chapel with the Guard cavalry); Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky has him place the Guard artillery on the Augezd heights in person
Retakes Telnitz for good

Follows Bagration's withdrawal toward Rausnitz with Suchet (Schönhals; Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky); the Allied report has a French line from the Rausnitz post house southward. The route drawn, east toward Krzenowitz, is this map's: no reading gives it
